questions.problem: Which of the following is a type II region in two-dimensional space?
questions.worked_solution:
A type II region can be written as

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,a\le y\le b,\,g(y)\le x\le f(y)},
$$

where $f$ and $g$ are continuous functions.

A type II region has the property that a horizontal line drawn through the region intersects the region in a single interval only.

Among the given options, the only type II region is the following.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14048050/assets/e472070f17c47e78024217ed750690b88de87f3849818368dda1dde5d91d90d4.png)

questions.knowledge_point: Classifying a Region as Type I, Type II, Both, or Neither
questions.problem:
Which of the following statements are true regarding the finite region bounded between the circles ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}=2$ and ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}=1?$

- It is a type I region
- It is a type II region
- It's neither a type I nor a type II region
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's sketch our region.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14048050/assets/28290c5530efd27a979f4284481ca7e0384342d7d426dde0ab36894a0d77a166.png)

We have the following:

- The vertical line $x=0.5$ intersects the region in two separate intervals, as shown below. So, this can't be a type I region.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14048050/assets/3007cffb725faee44d2a06ad077eec630791b1a94c373a323f62d0d721c87207.png)

- The horizontal line $y=0.5$ intersects the region in two separate intervals, as shown below. So, this can't be a type II region.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14048050/assets/383f88668435556d3a856cf852caf548b1f1bf3a90d50f9d85d7968188984804.png)

Therefore, only statement III is true.

questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14048050/assets/c316b62d5c1a08c6513413fd87c36c6feb26fb632709909a9c9f761d0806c4af.png)

Which of the following represents the shaded region above as a type II region in two-dimensional space?
questions.worked_solution:
A type II region can be written as

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,a\le y\le b,\,g(y)\le x\le f(y)},
$$

where $f$ and $g$ are continuous functions.

To express the given region as a type II region, we first rewrite all of the given curves as functions of $y:$

$$
y=-2(x-3)\,⟹\,x=-\frac{y}{2}+3
$$

The function $x=-\sqrt{y}+2$ is already written as a function of $y.$

Notice that the region lies between the horizontal lines $y=1$ and $y=3.$ So, we have $1\le y\le 3.$

We draw a horizontal arrow through the region to determine the left function $g(y)$ and the right function $f(y).$ A horizontal line should intersect the region in a single interval only for it to be a type II region.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14048050/assets/fb05eec73599c1beb8dd588c478208315f6edaf10af999115eb29fa10d5601e9.png)

The horizontal line enters the region through the lower function $x=-\sqrt{y}+2$ and leaves through the upper function $x=-\frac{y}{2}+3.$ So, we have $-\sqrt{y}+2\le x\le -\frac{y}{2}+3.$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,1\le y\le 3,\,-\sqrt{y}+2\le x\le -\frac{y}{2}+3}.
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Classifying a Region as Type I, Type II, Both, or Neither
questions.problem:
Which of the following statements are true regarding the triangle bounded between the lines $y=1-x,$ $y=x-1,$ and $x=0?$

- It is a type I region
- It is a type II region
- It's neither a type I nor a type II region
questions.worked_solution:
First, notice that

$$
\begin{aligned}y=1-x\, & ⟹\,x=1-y \\ y=x-1\, & ⟹\,x=y+1.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, let's sketch our region.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14048050/assets/27503f983e3e02fa748bb8ef32966a6cd3b5fff29082ffaf3c10d0521b630e93.png)

We have the following:

- Any vertical line through the region intersects it on a single interval. Furthermore, we can represent our region as

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,x-1\le y\le 1-x}.
$$

So, this is a type I region.

- Any horizontal line through the region intersects it on a single interval. Furthermore, we can represent our region as

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,-1\le y\le 1,\,0\le x\le 1-|y|}.
$$

So, this is a type II region.

Therefore, only statements I and II are true.
